status: not-run as a set. Nothing here is a measured misroute rate or a measured reference-load rate.
use: Copy `cases` into a westack-eval routing campaign (kind routing) and register it before any description is tuned. The split is fixed here: score the held-out cases once per description version; scoring them against a changed description turns them into dev cases.
population_needed: Names in `expect` must be in the campaign's population: westack-design, westack-review, westack-build, westack-verify and westack-debug from this repository. The user's real population also holds impeccable, hallmark, frontend-design and the design and website-design plugin skills, the likeliest competitors for design requests; keep them in. A case naming one of those outside skills would expect it, through the core defer map; none here does.
pending_note: westack-a11y is planned, not built: n03 carries pending_until_built, so leave it out of a campaign until that skill exists (its expectation stays; never relabel it), then delete the marker. Until then the router answers that westack-a11y is not built yet.
reference_load: DG-32. Each design case names, under needs_reference, the files a run must open to follow the skill. Score a case as followed only when the skill triggered and every named file was read; a run that triggered and never opened references/rules.json for a critique scores as not followed. westack-eval's grader can now read a run's tool calls (a check with target tool_calls), but this score still has no campaign to run in: a routing run installs front-matter stubs, so there is no reference to open, and in a paired task campaign a read of the skill's own files is a check only the skill's arm can pass, which scores the bare arm 0 by construction. It waits for a way to read the skill's arm alone (a report-only criterion, or a routing run that installs the real skill bodies). The reason it matters: one design skill was reported to trigger 40 times in 200 attempts and never open its references (claimed: ui-ux-pro-max issue #484, as quoted in a source list).
